Kansas City website design has a wrinkle most cities do not: the metro is split down the middle by a state line, and plenty of local businesses work both sides of it every week. A plumber based in Waldo takes calls from Prairie Village. A landscaper in Lenexa mows lawns in the Northland. A customer in Overland Park and a customer in Brookside both say they live in Kansas City, and both are right, but they search differently and they check different licenses.

If you searched web design Kansas City MO and landed here, Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites that sort this out in plain words. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas, you see a free demo first, and the prices are one time: $497, $997 or $1,997.

State Line Road runs through your customer list

State Line Road is exactly what it sounds like, and people in the metro cross it without thinking. KCUR, the local public radio station, has reported on residents who live on one side and cross over to work, shop and eat on the other. One longtime Overland Park resident put it simply: he looks at KC as one metropolitan area.

That is true for daily life and false for paperwork. Missouri and Kansas set different rules, and each city on each side sets its own. A website that ignores this either leaves out half the customers or confuses them. A customer in Brookside and a customer in Olathe want the same thing from your site: proof that you cover their side.

Same metro, different rules on each side

These are the differences that change what a small business website should say. Check the current rules with each office; this is a starting map, not legal advice.

TopicMissouri sideKansas side
City governmentKansas City, Missouri reaches into four counties: Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass.Kansas City, Kansas has been governed together with Wyandotte County since 1997, as the Unified Government.
Business licenseAnyone doing business in KCMO needs a city business license, renewed each year, with a zoning clearance first.Each city sets its own rules: Overland Park, Olathe and Lenexa are separate governments.
Contractor licensingKCMO requires a residential building contractor license to pull permits.Johnson County and most of its cities run a joint contractor license program; some cities, such as Prairie Village, also require their own city license.
What your site should sayThe KCMO neighborhoods and Missouri towns you serve, and your city license where it applies.The Kansas cities you serve by name, and the Johnson County or city license where it applies.

One helpful detail: KCMO says it built its residential contractor program to be comparable with Johnson County's and Independence's, so a residential builder exam passed in either of those places does not have to be retaken for KCMO. Your website does not need to explain any of that. It just needs to be accurate about which licenses you hold and where.

Kansas City website design by neighborhood and suburb

Inside Kansas City, Missouri, people identify with their part of town. The Crossroads Arts District downtown is known for galleries, studios and its First Fridays. The River Market, along the Missouri River, grew up around its historic marketplace. Westport is one of the city's oldest districts, known for restaurants and nightlife. Brookside and Waldo, to the south, are walkable neighborhoods of local shops and restaurants. North of the river, the Northland is an informal name usually taken to mean Clay and Platte counties, part of it inside KCMO and part of it not.

Across State Line, the suburbs are cities with their own names and their own searches: Overland Park, Olathe, Lenexa, Leawood, Shawnee, Prairie Village. Johnson County keeps adding people; FOX4 reported it grew by about 6,074 residents from 2024 to 2025. A customer there types "electrician Olathe," not "electrician Kansas City."

Good website design in Kansas City has to account for both habits, so the site for a business that serves both sides has a simple shape. The home page says Kansas City and names both states. Each area you want work from gets its own page, written about that area: the neighborhoods, how quickly you can get there, which license applies. The Pro package includes ten of these city pages. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and builds a page for each town and service pair the research says is worth having, usually 30 to 60 pages, in waves with the first live inside two weeks.

Why the town name matters to Google

Google says three things mainly decide its local results: relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is measured from the searcher, or from the place named in the search. When someone in Lenexa searches for a service, a business whose site and Google Business Profile say Lenexa clearly is a better match than one that says only "Kansas City metro." No web designer can promise where you will rank. A clear page for each town you serve is something you can control.

Free business help on both sides

KCSourceLink, housed at the UMKC Innovation Center, is a free network that connects small businesses with resource organizations across the 18-county Kansas City region, in both states. It is a good first call for loans, mentoring and training, and it costs nothing for the business owner. For KCMO licensing questions, the city's BizCare office publishes a step by step registration guide.

Common questions

How much does Kansas City web design cost?

Quotes around the metro range widely, and plenty of firms will not give one until after a meeting. Our prices are printed: $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for Pro with ten pages and ten city pages, and $1,997 for Agency, which starts with keyword research across your area. All are one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates run $49 a month, or are included while you keep the AI agent.

Do you do web design in Kansas City, MO and Kansas City, Kansas?

Yes, and in the suburbs on both sides. Kansas City, Missouri and Kansas City, Kansas are different cities in different states, and the Kansas one is governed together with Wyandotte County. If you serve both, each should get its own page that says so, rather than one page that blurs them together.

Is there a Kansas City web design company that also does SEO?

We handle the search setup that a small business site needs: page titles and descriptions, a sitemap submitted to Google, schema markup, and on Pro, Google Business Profile setup and city pages written for each town. That is Kansas City web design and SEO done together. We do not sell monthly ranking campaigns, and nobody can honestly promise you a ranking.

Should my contractor website list my Missouri and Kansas licenses separately?

Usually, yes. Licensing and permits differ by state and by city or county: Kansas City, Missouri has its own contractor licensing, and Johnson County, Kansas runs a county contractor license program that most of its cities use, sometimes alongside a city license. Put the license details for each side on the pages for that side, worded exactly as your license reads, so a homeowner checking you out finds the right one.

Can a web designer outside Kansas City build my site?

Yes. The work happens by phone, email and shared links. What you give up is meeting in person. Dominion Web Design Pro builds from East Texas, and the free demo lets you judge the work on your own phone before you spend anything.
